judgment.rationale: Both are Knowledge Objectives at the same grain and same coordinate (Grade P3, rank 2) within P3 Unit 4 'Fractions having a numerator less than or equal to 10'. The first states the conceptual meaning of denominator (number of equal parts a whole is divided into) and numerator (how many parts are considered); its LCs make both explicit. The second requires using drawings or real objects to compare fractions with the same denominator using <, >, = — a comparison that rests precisely on interpreting the fixed denominator as equal-part size and the differing numerators as counts of those parts. This is a pair-specific conceptual-to-applied extension, so proficiency in the meaning of numerator/denominator substantively supports success in comparing same-denominator fractions, justifying same-rank developmental direction first_to_second rather than mere shared-unit or shared-token coincidence. Evidence is limited: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the visible statement text and LCs.
